**The Whispering Trees**

In the quietest corners of the world, where the air hums with the secrets of forgotten things, there stands a grove of trees that whisper. Not in the way the wind rustles leaves, but in a language older than words—a murmur of roots and sap, of time curling back on itself like smoke.

The villagers call them the *Memory Trees*. They say if you press your ear to the bark, you can hear echoes of the past: a child’s laughter from a century ago, the sigh of a lover who never returned, the last breath of a dying star. Some claim the trees remember everything, that they hold the weight of every sorrow and joy ever felt beneath their branches.

But the trees do not speak to just anyone. They choose their listeners carefully, as if testing whether a soul is heavy enough to carry the weight of their stories. A woman once sat beneath the oldest oak for three days, her fingers tracing the grooves in the bark, until the tree finally sighed and let her hear the voice of her mother, long gone. A man, desperate for answers, pressed his forehead to the trunk and heard only silence—until he realized the silence itself was the answer.

No one knows how the trees came to be. Some say they grew from the tears of the first gods; others believe they are the last remnants of a world that existed before ours. The truth, if there is one, is buried deep in their roots, tangled in the earth like a secret too heavy to lift.

And so the trees stand, patient and eternal, whispering to those who dare to listen. But be careful—some stories are not meant to be heard. Some memories are better left in the dark.
